Support & Pricing

On this page

Cart Booking Component NEW ​

The AvailabilityMultiResults Livewire component is a cart-based booking surface for a single Entry. Instead of booking one date range and one rate at a time, the visitor can pick quantities per rate, add those selections to a running booking, change the dates and add more, and finally check out everything as a single reservation.

This is ideal for excursions, tours, classes, or any product where a customer books several units (or several dates) in one go. For the simpler one-rate / one-date flow, use the Availability Results component instead.

Component basics ​

Pair the component with an Availability Search instance so the visitor can pick dates and quantities. In its most basic form:

antlers
<livewire:availability-search :rates="true" :any-rate="true" />
<livewire:availability-multi-results :entry="id" />

Because the component is rate-driven, the availability-search it is paired with should run with :rates="true" and :any-rate="true" so that every rate is returned for the searched dates.

A common pattern is to loop a collection and render a multi-results block per entry:

antlers
{{ collection:excursions }}
    <livewire:availability-search :entry="id" :rates="true" :any-rate="true" />
    <livewire:availability-multi-results :entry="id" />
{{ /collection:excursions }}

Both the <livewire:...> and the Antlers {{ livewire:... }} syntaxes work.

Component properties ​

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
entrystringnone - requiredNeeds to be a Statamic Entry ID. The Entry the cart books against. Passed as the mount parameter.
ratesbooleantrueDefaults to true here: the component is rate-driven and always resolves per-rate labels and prices.
showExtrasboolean or stringfalseShow the Extras component inside the cart panel. Set to true for all extras, or a filter slug. (more information below)
showOptionsboolean or stringfalseShow the Options component inside the cart panel. Set to true for all options, or a filter slug. (more information below)
overrideRatesarray[]Override the rate_id => label map instead of resolving labels from the Rate model.
viewstring"availability-multi-results"You can override the view that is used to render the component. Expects a name.blade.php file in the /resources/views/vendor/statamic-resrv/livewire folder.

NO showRates PROP

Unlike the Availability Collection component, availability-multi-results does not have a showRates property. It always renders every available rate with its own quantity picker.

The cart flow ​

The component renders three areas that work together:

  1. Per-rate quantity pickers. Once the visitor searches, each available rate is shown with its label, the per-unit price, an optional cancellation policy label, and - / + buttons to set a quantity. Availability is always queried at quantity 1 so the displayed prices are per unit; the customer picks the quantity afterwards.
  2. Add to booking. When at least one rate has a quantity greater than zero, an "Add to booking" button appears. Clicking it pushes every selected rate (with its dates, rate, quantity, and price) into the cart and resets the pickers.
  3. Your booking. Once the cart has any selections, a "Your booking" panel lists every line item (rate label, quantity, date range, and line total) with a remove button, a running Total, a Clear link, and a "Book now" button.

Because the dates come from the paired availability-search, the visitor can change the dates and add more selections to the same cart. Each "Add to booking" appends to the existing cart rather than replacing it, so a single booking can span several different date ranges and rates.

Clicking Book now validates the whole cart, creates the reservation, and redirects the visitor to the Checkout page.

Extras and Options (Optional) ​

Like the Availability Results component, you can display the Entry's Extras and Options inline. Here they render inside the "Your booking" cart panel and their pricing is recalculated against every selection in the cart:

antlers
<livewire:availability-multi-results :entry="id" :show-extras="true" :show-options="true" />

The selected extras and options are carried over to the Checkout component as usual.

How the reservation is structured ​

When the visitor checks out, the cart is converted into a reservation that the normal checkout flow understands without any special handling:

  • One parent reservation is created. It stores the overall total price and the overall date span.
  • One child reservation per cart selection is created, each with its own dates, rate, quantity, and price.

The event-driven reservation lifecycle handles the rest: availability is decreased per child when the reservation is created, and increased again per child if it expires or is cancelled. The Checkout component treats the parent reservation exactly like a normal single reservation, so the whole cart is paid for in one transaction.

DATABASE MIGRATION

This feature adds a price column to the resrv_child_reservations table. The migration runs automatically with the package migrations; existing child reservation rows get price = null.

How the cart is scoped to one entry ​

The cart lives in the session and is scoped to the Entry that owns it. Three session keys are used:

  • resrv-search: the shared search state (dates, quantity, rate).
  • resrv-multi-selections: the cart itself.
  • resrv-multi-cart-entry: which Entry owns the cart.

When you visit a different Entry's multi-results page, the component detects that the persisted cart belongs to another Entry (or to none) and starts clean, so a cart never leaks between Entries. After checkout the cart and its owner are cleared, while any selected extras and options are left in the session for the Checkout component to copy onto the reservation.

Customizing ​

The main template file can be found at /resources/views/vendor/statamic-resrv/livewire/availability-multi-results.blade.php. Publish the views first if you haven't already (either during installation or by running php artisan vendor:publish --tag=resrv-checkout-views), then edit the file to choose which elements to display and how to style them.

Translations ​

The component uses these frontend translation keys, which you can override as described in the Languages page:

KeyDefault
addToBookingAdd to booking
yourBookingYour booking
totalTotal
clearClear
bookNowBook now
pleaseSelectRateToBookPlease select a rate to book
pleaseSelectDatesPlease select dates to search for availability.
noAvailabilityNo availability
searchErrorSearch error
youAreTooLateYou are too late!

The optional cancellation policy label also uses the cancellation keys (nonRefundable, freeCancellationUntilDate) documented on the Rates page.
